solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get coat altered in rural building

indicators.note: altered says the letters of the preceding two words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has their coat tailored in a farmhouse or village dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically found in the countryside.

clue.text: Reminder of broadcast line

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out over the airwaves, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue

explanation.surface: A prompt for an actor delivered over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that QUEUE (line) is heard, giving the like-sounding word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal or prompt, something that reminds a performer to speak or act.

clue.text: Blunder allowed in one of three

parts.note: to trip is to stumble or make a mistake

explanation.surface: A permitted error committed by one of a set of triplets.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born at a single birth.

clue.text: Book finally shortened

indicators.note: shortened tells us to cut off the final letter of the phrase given

explanation.surface: A book has at last been abridged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' removes the last T from AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound volume of maps, so a kind of book.

clue.text: Serious listener, home later

indicators.note: later says the home piece comes after the listener piece in the answer

parts.note: the ear is the organ one listens with
a nest is a home, for birds or figuratively

explanation.surface: A grave-faced listener who will head home afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave in manner, a synonym of serious.

clue.text: Instant credit

definitions.meaning: a ... is a moment, as in 'just a ...'
on credit, an informal British usage

explanation.surface: Credit available straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Tick is informal for both a brief moment and a deferred-payment arrangement.

clue.text: By the sound of it, yarns for formal wear

indicators.note: this phrase asks for a word heard the same as the synonym that follows

explanation.surface: Stories that, when heard, suggest evening dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tails is short for a tailcoat, the long-backed jacket worn with white tie.

clue.text: Tell niece, working, to see customers

indicators.note: working means being processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to a busy niece to attend to the shop's patrons.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of clients or patrons of a business.

clue.text: Domestic servant getting new start is friendly

indicators.note: the servant word has its opening letter swapped for a different one

parts.note: a menial is a household servant doing lowly work

explanation.surface: A servant gets a fresh beginning and becomes good-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not clued; crossings fix it as G.
explanation.definitionFit: Genial means warm and friendly in manner.

clue.text: Grape is beset by wet weather

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the short word goes inside the weather word

explanation.surface: A grape crop is spoiled by rain.
explanation.walkthrough: A raisin is a dried grape, and the French word for grape.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, so the clue uses the fruit itself loosely.

clue.text: One hoping you buy second drinks for each child

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Someone buys a second round for every youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesperson wants customers to purchase, so they hope you will buy.

clue.text: Flavour of pantries, after refurbishment, captivating Mike

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one piece is placed inside the other
refurbishment remodels something, so the letters of pantries are rearranged

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The taste noticed in kitchen storerooms after a makeover, which charms Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after refurbishment' turns PANTRIES into SPEARINT, and 'captivating' holds M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a mint used to flavour gum, sweets and toothpaste.

clue.text: Busy, cite changes in hours, constant

indicators.note: in places the anagram inside the two single letters

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, notably the speed of light

indicators.note: changes means the letters of cite are altered in order

explanation.surface: A busy person citing changes to their hours and remaining steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' scrambles 'cite', and 'in' puts the result between the two single letters; c is the physics symbol for the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic means full of frantic activity, a synonym of busy.

clue.text: No-good prig in cult — who's to blame?

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word goes inside cult
no good means the letter for good is dropped from prig

explanation.surface: A worthless prig in a sect, asking who is responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the usual abbreviation for good; 'No-good' strips it from PRIG, leaving PRI.
explanation.definitionFit: The culprit is the person responsible for a wrong, the one who is to blame.

clue.text: This decorative item cheers? Not so much, on reflection

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: reflection is a mirror image, so the combined letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: An ornament that, looking back, seems to applaud less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns only the 'Not so much' word; TA is British informal thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is an ornamental tuft of threads hanging from cushions, curtains or caps.

clue.text: Begin extremely late causing alarm

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outer letters, of late

explanation.surface: Starting at the very last minute leads to panic.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden fright, to alarm them.

clue.text: Poisonous reptile disconcerts nude no end

parts.note: to rattle someone is to disconcert them

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A venomous snake endlessly upsets a naked person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is a venomous American viper with a rattle on its tail.

clue.text: Watch maybe as millions lodged in bank

indicators.note: lodged in means placed inside, so the letter sits within the bank word

parts.note: a bank is a row or tier, as of seats or oars

explanation.surface: Money in the millions deposited in a bank, watched over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but means a row, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one example of a device that measures time, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Boy with nothing on a Polynesian state

explanation.surface: A lad wearing nothing, arriving in a Pacific island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an independent island country in the South Pacific, part of Polynesia.

clue.text: Seethe as whiskey taken from bather?

indicators.note: taken from means the letter is removed from the swimmer word

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bather fumes after their whisky is snatched away.
explanation.definitionFit: To simmer is to be close to boiling, hence to seethe with suppressed anger.

clue.text: Saying nothing about a temperature change

indicators.note: about means around, so the silent word surrounds the inserted letters

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet on the subject of climate change.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form or nature, to change.

clue.text: Cask from Soviet Union

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of the two words

explanation.surface: A barrel that came out of the USSR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large beer or wine barrel.

clue.text: Strong reaction in prison

definitions.meaning: a commotion, a big public reaction

explanation.surface: A sharp backlash inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir means both a commotion and, in slang, a jail.

clue.text: Vehicle collecting editor on way back or one used in transaction?

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the vehicle word holds the other piece
on the way back means heading in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A vehicle picks up an editor on the return trip, or is part-exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' reverses the editor's abbreviation, and 'collecting' holds it inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item, often a car, handed over as part payment for a new one.
